stories.title: Colombia earthquake rescue efforts enter second day as death toll reaches 164
stories.summary: Rescuers in western Colombia worked through the night and into Tuesday searching for survivors beneath the wreckage after a powerful 7.4 magnitude earthquake devastated parts of the country’s coffee-growing region on Monday. At least 164 people have been killed and authorities are warning the number of casualties could still climb.

stories.title: Spain’s Huelva blaze threatens homes, 800 evacuated amid severe drought
stories.summary: A massive wildfire in Spain’s Huelva province has forced 800 evacuations, burned around 20,000 hectares and comes during Europe’s worsening drought crisis.
stories.post: 📰 NEWS: Spain’s Huelva blaze threatens homes, 800 evacuated amid severe drought. A massive wildfire in Spain’s Huelva province has forced 800 evacuations, burned around 20,000 hectares and comes during Europe’s worsening drought crisis. Source: Africanews English.
article_sentences: Footage from Niebla and Valverde del Camino, in Spain's Huelva province, filmed on Monday 10 August 2026, shows firefighting helicopters dropping water on flames, plumes of smoke rising over the countryside, and evacuees gathered in a theatre in Zalamea la Real.
Welder Daniel Lopez said neighbours were terrified after homes came close to burning, with some destroyed.

More than 600 firefighters backed by 26 aircraft have battled the blaze since it broke out a week earlier, regional emergencies minister Antonio Sanz said, describing it as extremely difficult and dangerous with no forecast of it being controlled soon.
Around 20,000 hectares lie within the fire's perimeter, and evacuations now total roughly 800 people after officials ordered residents of El Madrono to leave on Monday.
The fire comes amid a severe wildfire season in Spain, following a 50,000-hectare blaze near Madrid in July and a fire that killed 14 people in Almeria.
Nearly all of mainland France and Switzerland recorded record drought in July, as Europe warms faster than any other continent, Copernicus data show.

stories.title: WHO: DRC Ebola outbreak began months before it was officially declared
stories.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the DR Congo began months before it was officially declared, the World Health Organization told a news conference in Bunia on Monday. It’s now the fastest growing Ebola outbreak on record.

stories.title: Europe’s total solar eclipse: the best place to see it and how to view it safely
stories.summary: Moon is due to pass directly between Earth and sun on Wednesday 12 August. Here’s all you need to know On Wednesday evening, millions of Europeans will experience a celestial treat: a solar eclipse. A wide band of north and central Spain, plus a sliver of Portugal and parts of Greenland and Iceland will experience a rare total eclipse. The light of the setting sun will be virtually blocked out across much of western Europe, including the UK, France, Belgium, Switzerland and northern Italy. stories.title: Australia’s prime minister refuses to apologise to Japanese counterpart over melon gaffe
stories.summary: Anthony Albanese faces criticism after appearing to joke on a podcast about a gift of melons from Sanae Takaichi The Australian prime minister, Anthony Albanese, has rejected calls to apologise to Japan’s prime minister over a joke he made about melons on a satirical podcast, amid a media frenzy and accusations of sexual innuendo. Government MPs have defended the prime minister as criticism mounted over last month’s remarks, branded by the Coalition opposition as “grubby”. The assistant minister Pat Gorman told media: “I don’t know why we’re still talking about this.” Continue reading...
